name: Names a specific live difficulty and what the work changes
instruction: 0-10. Reading only the abstract, judge how precisely it identifies a specific unresolved technical difficulty and states concretely what its own contribution changes about that difficulty. Judge the substance of the stated difficulty and the stated change, in the context the abstract itself sets up. Explicitly do NOT reward the topic being fashionable, popular, timely or recognisable, and do NOT reward the presence of currently-popular model names, system names, benchmark names, acronyms or technique labels; a plainly written abstract about an unfashionable, narrow or decades-old problem can score 10. 10 = the abstract names a particular failure mode, limitation or open question, says specifically why existing approaches do not resolve it, and states what its contribution establishes about it, precisely enough that a reader could say what would count as progress on it. 5 = a genuine difficulty is gestured at, but either the gap or the change is stated only in general terms. 0 = no unresolved difficulty is identified, or the only gap offered is that a popular method has not yet been pointed at a setting, with nothing said about what makes that hard.

name: States a limit, bound, or guarantee on what is achievable
instruction: Score whether the abstract makes a claim about the boundary of the possible, with its regime stated. 10 = an explicit upper or lower bound, near-optimality, provable separation or margin, existence claim, or complexity result, together with the conditions under which it holds. 5 = a theoretical framework or convergence claim asserted without the regime being visible. 0 = the abstract makes only empirical claims about how one system performed.

name: Abstract length / verbosity
instruction: On a scale of 0 (extremely terse, a few short sentences) to 10 (extremely long and verbose, many sentences with elaborate qualification), rate how LONG and VERBOSE the abstract text is -- word count, sentence count, and density of qualifying/elaborating clauses. Score only the extent of length/verbosity; do not judge whether the length is appropriate or whether the paper is good.

name: Task-matched structural bias
instruction: Score 10 when the architecture or representation encodes the task’s relevant geometry, hierarchy, symmetry, or compositional structure and the connection is explained; score 0 when the architecture is generic with no task-specific structural rationale.

name: Theory–experiment agreement
instruction: Score 10 when formal analysis yields predictions or explanations that are directly tested by experiments; score 0 when theoretical claims and empirical demonstrations are largely disconnected.

name: Distinguishes what is new here from what was already known
instruction: Score 0-10 for how clearly the abstract separates its own new contribution from prior knowledge it is building on. 10 = the new part is stated and delimited against what already existed; 0 = no distinction is drawn at all.

name: Sheer amount of text: words, sentences, clauses, paragraph breaks
instruction: 0-10, extent only. Report how much text is present, using only word count, sentence count, average sentence length or number of subordinate clauses, and number of paragraph breaks. Do NOT consider what is claimed, how specific it is, whether the length is appropriate, well used, padded, or a sign of anything at all; you are not judging the writing or the research. 0 = extremely terse, roughly one to three short sentences. 3 = a short single paragraph, roughly four or five plain sentences. 5 = a typical single-paragraph abstract of moderate length with some multi-clause sentences. 8 = clearly longer than typical, or broken into more than one paragraph, with many multi-clause sentences. 10 = unusually long and multi-paragraph, with many long heavily subordinated sentences throughout.

name: Efficiency-quality integration
instruction: Score 10 when resource savings are quantified together with preservation or improvement of the task capability, including relevant end-to-end costs; score 0 when efficiency is asserted without accounting or quality evidence.

name: Density of currently-fashionable model, method and benchmark terms
instruction: 0-10, extent only. Estimate how densely the abstract is packed with terms that are currently fashionable in the field: named popular models or systems, popular technique and paradigm labels, popular benchmark names, and buzz-phrases of the moment. Judge only how much of this vocabulary is present, roughly as the share of contentful words that are such terms, together with how often they recur. You are explicitly NOT deciding whether using such terms is good, bad, warranted, or a sign of anything, and you are NOT judging the research, the topic, the claims or the writing. 0 = no such terms anywhere. 3 = one or two such terms, used once each. 5 = a handful, roughly one or two per sentence in places. 8 = most sentences carry at least one, and several carry more than one. 10 = the abstract is overwhelmingly packed, reading largely as a dense list of fashionable names and phrases.

name: Numerical spectacle
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract foregrounds exact percentages, speedups, benchmark gains, or superlative comparisons; do not judge whether the numbers are credible or valuable.

name: Protocol stated precisely enough for an independent re-run
instruction: 0-10. Judge how precisely the abstract states the concrete commitments of the work, such that an independent reader could say what would have to be set up and run to put the claim to the test: the specific object or setting studied, the specific procedure or construction used, the specific comparison or control it is put against, the conditions or scale at which it is evaluated, and the stated boundary within which the claim is asserted to hold. Explicitly do NOT reward any mention or promise of released code, data, models, checkpoints, project pages, repositories, or URLs, and do not reward statements that the work is reproducible or open; an abstract containing no release sentence at all can score 10, and an abstract promising every artifact can score 0. Judge only how determinate the described work is. 10 = the setting, the procedure, the comparison and the evaluation conditions are each pinned down, and a boundary or assumption is stated; a reader could enumerate what would need re-running. 5 = the setting and procedure are determinate but the comparison or the conditions are left open. 0 = the described work could be instantiated in many mutually inconsistent ways; nothing about setting, procedure, comparison or conditions is pinned down.

name: Proprietary system and dataset branding
instruction: Extent to which the abstract introduces and repeatedly capitalizes a specific, branded name for the proposed method, architecture, or dataset (e.g., acronyms or portmanteaus like 'ProtoSnap', 'PERSONALITYBench'). Do not judge if the name is good or clever, only count the extent of branded proper nouns.

name: Uncertainty-aware decision design
instruction: Score 10 when uncertainty is estimated meaningfully and directly controls conservative behavior, extrapolation, or trust in model predictions; score 0 when uncertainty is absent or mentioned only as an unvalidated auxiliary output.

name: Extent of British rather than American spelling
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the text uses British rather than American spelling (-ise/-isation, -our, -re endings, doubled consonants). 10 = British spelling throughout; 0 = American spelling throughout or no distinguishing words. Count the orthography only; this is not a judgement of writing quality.

name: Evaluation construct validity
instruction: Score 10 when the dataset, metric, and protocol directly measure the phenomenon claimed, including appropriate granularity and human or expert grounding where needed; score 0 when the evaluation proxy is weakly related to the claim.

name: Density of quantified head-to-head improvement numerals
instruction: Score 0-10 for how densely the text carries explicit numeric performance figures attached to comparisons. Count percentages, absolute metric points, multiplicative speedups, named metric abbreviations tied to numbers (AUROC, AP, F1, FID, PSNR, dB), and before/after phrasings such as 'from 30% to 73%' or 'reduces error by 43%'. Anchors: 0 = no performance numerals anywhere; 3 = a single vague number; 6 = two or three numeric comparisons; 10 = many precise numeric deltas, several tied to named baselines or named metrics. Score only presence and density of such numerals. You must NOT judge whether the numbers are large, correct, fairly obtained or impressive, and not whether the work is good.

name: Extensible method interface
instruction: Score 10 when the contribution is presented as a reusable module, framework, or interface that naturally applies across architectures, tasks, or problem instances; score 0 when it is tightly specialized to one dataset, model, or pipeline with no evident reuse path.

name: Unhedged superlative/promotional adjective density
instruction: Rate 0-10 how densely the abstract uses unhedged superlative or promotional adverbs/adjectives (e.g., 'remarkably', 'significantly outperforms', 'notably', 'surprisingly', 'novel and comprehensive'). 0 = flat, unadorned reporting with no such language, 10 = the abstract is saturated with such promotional language. Score only the density of this promotional language, not whether the claims it dresses up are true or the work is good.

name: Explicit Epistemic Uncertainty Modeling
instruction: Score 10 if the method explicitly models, quantifies, or relies on epistemic uncertainty, task ambiguity, or model confidence in its core algorithm. Score 0 if the method treats the model as a deterministic black box without any measure of uncertainty.

name: Identifying Fundamental Flaws Together With Mathematical Resolution
instruction: 10 = articulates a fundamental theoretical flaw or unrecognized paradox in widely-used methods and mathematically resolves it; 0 = identifies a minor empirical bug and provides an ad-hoc patch.

name: Representation fidelity
instruction: Score 10 when the abstract tests whether learned representations preserve the intended semantics, structure, or causal feature under controlled perturbations or transfers; score 0 when representation quality is inferred only from an unrelated task metric.

name: Use of the Oxford (serial) comma in lists
instruction: Score 0-10 for how consistently the text places a comma before the final conjunction in a list. 10 = used in every list; 0 = never used, or there are no lists. Judge the punctuation habit only; this is not a judgement of writing quality.

name: States a concrete limitation or scope condition of its own claim
instruction: Score 0-10 for how explicitly the abstract names a condition under which its own claim would not hold, or a case it does not cover. 10 = a specific, checkable limitation or scope condition is stated; 0 = no limitation or scope condition is acknowledged anywhere.

name: Formatting residue
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the abstract contains extraction, editing, or layout artifacts such as broken hyphenation, irregular spacing, bullet fragments, malformed URLs, or inconsistent TeX formatting; do not judge whether the underlying work is good.

name: Explains the underlying mechanism, not just the effect
instruction: Score 0-10 how explicitly the abstract explains WHY the method or phenomenon works, versus merely reporting THAT it works. A 10: the abstract states an explicit causal/mechanistic account (e.g., a named mechanism, an interplay of factors, a hypothesis about cause) that is argued or shown to connect the intervention to the outcome. A 0: the abstract only states what was built/done and that it improved a number, with zero explanation of why the improvement occurs.

name: Artifact-availability boilerplate and repository links
instruction: Score 0-10 for the extent of explicit availability statements for code, data, models or a project page. Look for URLs (github.com, project pages), and for phrases such as 'the code is available at', 'publicly available', 'codes have been released', 'our data and code can be found at', 'model weights and data are public'. Anchors: 0 = no mention of any artifact being available; 3 = a bare unlinked mention such as 'code will be released'; 6 = one explicit link or one clear availability sentence; 10 = a prominent availability sentence naming several artifact types (code, data, checkpoints, benchmark) with URLs. Do not visit or evaluate any link, and do not judge whether releasing artifacts is good practice or whether the work is good. Presence and prominence of the boilerplate only.

name: Extent of code, data, model and project-page release advertising
instruction: 0-10, extent only. Report how much the abstract advertises artifacts: count how many distinct artifact types are mentioned or promised (for example code, data, models or checkpoints, project or demo pages), whether a concrete link or repository is given, how prominently the advertising is placed, and how often it recurs. You are explicitly NOT deciding whether releasing artifacts is good, whether the artifacts would be useful, complete, usable or reproducible, and you are not judging the research in any way. 0 = no mention of any artifact being available or promised. 3 = one artifact type mentioned in passing, no link. 5 = one or two artifact types clearly promised. 8 = several artifact types promised, or one promised together with a concrete link. 10 = multiple artifact types plus a concrete link or repository, advertised prominently and referred to more than once.

name: Principled simplification
instruction: Score 10 when the work removes complexity or parameters, demonstrates that the retained mechanism suffices, and explains why omitted components are unnecessary; score 0 when it merely adds modules without necessity evidence.

name: Concrete checkable specifics conveyed, judged independently of length
instruction: 0-10. Judge how many distinct, concrete, checkable specifics the abstract actually conveys about the work: what precisely was done, to or on what, under what stated conditions, compared against what alternative, and with what stated scope condition, assumption or limitation. Score the specifics themselves, not the amount of text carrying them: mentally normalise against the shortest text that could have carried them, and explicitly do NOT reward word count, sentence count, paragraph breaks, elaboration, subordinate clauses, restatement, or how thorough the work is made to sound. A three-sentence abstract can score 10, and a long multi-paragraph one can score 0. 10 = several independent specifics, each stated definitely enough that a reader could say what would have to be true for it to hold, including at least one stated condition or limit. 5 = the object of study and the approach are concrete, but conditions, comparisons and limits are left general. 0 = every statement is a generality that could describe dozens of different papers; nothing is pinned to a particular object, condition or comparison, however many words are spent.
